title: Decision Watch Lifecycle
purpose: Create, update, pause, resume, and close company-scoped decision watches with an explicit revision and event contract.

operations.create: Creates an active watch at revision 0 when the company/watch key is unused.
operations.update: Changes the condition or lifecycle timing fields of an active or paused watch.
operations.pause: Moves an active watch to paused and clears its scheduled evaluation timestamp.
operations.resume: Moves a non-expired paused watch to active and clears its scheduled evaluation timestamp.
operations.close: Soft-closes an active or paused watch; closed watches are terminal.

transition_policy.company_id: Immutable scope key and the only company boundary.
transition_policy.decision_subject_id: Set at creation and remains immutable.
transition_policy.revision: Every changing command carries expected_revision; a host compare-and-swap commits expected_revision + 1.
transition_policy.condition_update: Clears last_triggered_at and next_evaluation_at when the condition changes.
transition_policy.interval_update: Clears next_evaluation_at so the host scheduler can recalculate its schedule.
transition_policy.remove: Represented by close; preserve the watch record for audit and history.

persistence_contract.command_id: Stable host-generated idempotency identifier; retries must reuse the same identifier and payload.
persistence_contract.fingerprint: The engine hashes a canonical JSON representation of the complete command. The host checks the company-scoped command receipt before loading mutable watch state and checks again atomically during commit.
persistence_contract.transaction: Atomically check the command receipt and expected revision, write the watch revision and lifecycle event, then store the command fingerprint and result receipt.
persistence_contract.retry: The same command ID and fingerprint returns the stored result as duplicate; reusing an ID with a different fingerprint returns conflict.
persistence_contract.create_conflict: expected_revision null requires that the watch key is absent.
persistence_contract.update_conflict: A revision mismatch returns conflict without writing the proposed watch or event.
persistence_contract.unchanged: Same-state transitions and equal-value updates may record a command receipt without increasing the watch revision.

invariants: The lifecycle engine proposes watch state; it does not own durable storage or list queries.
The host authorizes who may create or change a watch before calling the engine.
The engine never sends notifications, starts decision runs, or executes recommended actions.
Lifecycle events include changed field names but omit condition expected values and source payloads.
Every plan and event carries authority_effect none.
host_owned_components: watch listing and durable company-scoped storage
authorization, user identity, and command receipt retention
transactional revision compare-and-swap and event persistence
scheduler updates, signal routing, notifications, and execution
